subject: MSA & Order Form: SLA rollforward and maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Daniel Price <daniel.price@auroratech.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@auroratech.com
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: SLA uptime / credits / scheduled maintenance

Hi Chloe / Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA + Order Form. We've looped in procurement and legal on our side. A few items jumped out from our security & SRE review that we'd like to resolve before we move to signatures:

- Uptime target currently at 99.95% (regional) — can you confirm whether measurement is per-region or global aggregate? Our compliance team prefers region-level measurement.
- Service credit formula: draft uses (Monthly Downtime / Total Minutes) * (Monthly Fee) — procurement asked for an example calculation and a monthly cap. Can Redwood propose a cap?
- Response times: we need P1/P2 definitions to align with our incident taxonomy.
- Maintenance windows: proposal currently allows rolling maintenance with 6-hour windows. We need clarity on blackout windows (payroll and EMEA peak hours) and whether customers can request maintenance freezes.

I've attached our redlines (AuroraTech_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Can we get an internal sync with ops + legal from Redwood to walk through the proposed edits? Ideally this week.

Daniel
Daniel Price
Director, Infrastructure & Security
AuroraTech

Attachments: AuroraTech_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Price <daniel.price@auroratech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: SLA uptime / credits / scheduled maintenance

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear summary and for the redlines.

We can absolutely do a focused sync. Proposed plan:
1) Internal quick review (ops + legal) today to identify hard constraints.
2) 30‑minute triage call with AuroraTech tomorrow to walk the remaining items and agree on concrete wording.
3) Produce an updated Order Form (v3.1) with an example credit calculation and a recommended monthly cap.

Jonas, Marissa — can you confirm availability for a 30m call tomorrow (12:30pm PT / 3:30pm ET)? I will share the maintenance matrix and include an annotated example of the credit math.

High-level notes for the internal review (no need to reply-all yet):
- On uptime measurement: if we do region-level measurement, we need to be explicit about the aggregation window and any downsampling logic for multi-az models.
- Credit cap: business normally proposes a 5% monthly cap; legal may push that down or ask for a staircase approach.
- Maintenance carveouts: ops prefers scheduled maintenance windows that minimize customer impact, but some upgrades require longer exclusive windows. Need to list exceptions.

I'll set the call if you confirm times.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: maintenance_window_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Price <daniel.price@auroratech.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: SLA uptime / credits / scheduled maintenance

Chloe / team / Daniel — thanks, looping in a few legal talking points here before the call: 

On the credit formula and cap:
- Proposed wording: "Service Credits = (Downtime Minutes / Total Monthly Minutes) * Monthly Service Fee" with an illustrative example appended.
- Cap: legal would accept a 5% monthly credit cap as a starting point for commercial deals; for strategic customers we can tier or waive.
- Staircase: if AuroraTech prefers a progressive scale (e.g., 0.5% for <1% downtime, up to 5% for >3%), we can draft a table.

On uptime measurement:
- We recommend region-level measurement (explicitly name the region ID + AZ aggregation rules). Add a definition section: "Availability measurement shall be calculated at the region level using the Redwood telemetry aggregation window (UTC daily buckets)."

On response times (definitions):
- P1 (Platform down/no response for production workloads): initial response within 1 hour, remediation SLA to be agreed operationally;
- P2 (Degraded performance but service responsive): initial response within 4 hours;
- P3 (Non-urgent/config/feature requests): initial response within 2 business days.

On scheduled maintenance and carveouts:
- Legal wants the Order Form to state: "Scheduled maintenance windows will be announced at least 7 calendar days in advance where practical. Maintenance will be limited to a standard window of up to 6 hours per event; total scheduled maintenance will not exceed 12 hours/month unless mutually agreed."
- Ops will want exceptions for emergency patching and driver upgrades — propose adding an "Emergency Maintenance" carveout with a different notice requirement.

Open asks for AuroraTech (please confirm during call):
1) Is region-level availability acceptable?
2) Do you want a monthly cap as percent of fees or an absolute cap?
3) Are there blackout windows AuroraTech requires — list local times/regions.

I will draft language for the Order Form and bring the staircase credit table to the call.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Sales Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Price <daniel.price@auroratech.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: SLA uptime / credits / scheduled maintenance

Adding ops perspective before the call. Quick notes:

- Maintenance duration: some infra-level maintenance (kernel, CUDA) can require up to 8 hours for safe sequencing on certain instance families; constraining every event to 6 hours will require more frequent, smaller events which can increase risk. Suggest we keep a standard target of 6 hours but allow "extended maintenance" up to 12 hours with advance notice and coordination.

- Blackout windows: we can honor customer-requested blackout windows for scheduled maintenance for critical payroll/settlement periods, but these must be requested at least 14 days in advance and will limit our ability to apply certain safety updates during those times.

- Degradation handling: instead of full outage during maintenance, we can offer degraded throughput fallback — i.e., throttle model concurrency per-tenant while maintaining token generation capability. This reduces customer pain and minimizes credit exposure. Recommend adding this as an explicit mitigation step in the maintenance section.

I'll prepare an ops appendix with examples of maintenance types, expected durations, and the mitigation options we can apply.

—Jonas Weber
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: SLA uptime / credits / scheduled maintenance

Thanks — that all helps.

AuroraTech responses:
1) Region-level measurement is acceptable. Please include explicit region IDs in the definition section.
2) Preference for a percent cap (5% monthly) but we're open to the staircase table Marissa mentioned.
3) Blackout windows: Payroll batch run — last Friday of month 22:00–02:00 UTC; EMEA peak 07:00–11:00 UTC weekdays. We'll formally provide a calendar of blackout days after the call.

We accept the proposed compromise around a standard 6-hour window and an "extended maintenance" carveout with advance notice. The degraded-throughput mitigation sounds like a great option — please include it in the maintenance appendix.

Next step: can Redwood produce v3.1 order form with the example credit calc, the staircase table (if you propose one), and the ops appendix (maintenance types + mitigation) and share a DocuSign link? If that looks good we can aim to sign next week.

Daniel

----
Daniel Price
Director, Infrastructure & Security
AuroraTech
